title: Sara Duterte's former staff being held, forced to sign document, says VP camp
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte has received information about her former household help allegedly being held against their will and being forced to sign a document, Atty. Paolo Panelo said Tuesday.
byline: LLANESCA T. PANTI, GISELLE OMBAY, GMA News

blocks.text: Published November 17, 2026 1:15pm
Vice President Sara Duterte has received information about her former household help allegedly being held against their will and being forced to sign a document, Atty. Paolo Panelo said Tuesday.

In a Facebook post, Panelo, Duterte's spokesperson, said the Vice President received a message "from what appeared to be the account of a former household staff member" at 11:19 pm on Monday, November 16.

“The message contained a desperate plea for help and rescue in Manila. The sender claimed to be in the custody or under the control of certain individuals who allegedly told them about a threat to their life. The former staff member further narrated that they were being forced to sign a document, which they had refused to execute,” he said.

He added the incident is similar to what happened to Duterte's former media officer, Jefry Tupas, who earlier accused the National Bureau of Investigation of forcing him to come to Manila after being told that there is a threat to his life.

NBI chief Melvin Matibag earlier said that Tupas was the source of information about threats to his security. Tupas disputed this saying NBI agents were the ones who went to his home in North Cotabato in September.
Panelo said the whereabouts of the former household staff member remain unknown, "and their safety and well-being have yet to be independently verified."

"We are deeply concerned that this incident may be part of what we believe to be a relentless campaign by the Marcos administration, utilizing state institutions like the NBI, against the Vice President,” he added.
Probe needed
Malacañang, on the other hand, said that such claims should be investigated to determine its accuracy.
“Ang pag-iimbestiga sa nasabing kwento kung may katotohanan ay nararapat lamang,” Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro said in a statement.
(It’s only fitting to investigate the claims to determine if there is any truth to it.)
Regardless, Castro emphasized that the President is currently busy with the ASEAN Summit.

“Buhos ang oras ng Pangulo sa pagtatrabaho para sa ikakaunlad ng bansa at sa pagpapatibay ng magandang ugnayan sa mga member states ng ASEAN at mga dialogue partners. Pagpapaayos ng ekonomiya, solusyon sa usaping enerhiya, teknolohiya, agrikultura, at edukasyon ang tinututukan ng ating Pangulo,” she said.

(The President is dedicating his time to the nation’s development and strengthening positive relations with ASEAN member-states and dialogue partners. He is focusing on improving the economy, as well as addressing issues related to energy, technology, agriculture, and education.)
Castro also stressed that Marcos does not resort to doing such.

“Hindi po gawain sa panahon ngayon ang gumawa ng intriga at magplanta ng ebidensya kung saan sanay at hasa ang Duterte administration at ito naman ay inamin noon pa ni dating Pangulong Duterte sa harapan ng media,” she added.

(The administration does not stir up such allegations or plant evidence—tactics in which the Duterte administration is well-versed and highly skilled, as former President Duterte himself previously admitted before the media.)
GMA News Online has reached out to the NBI for comment and will publish it as soon as it becomes available.
The Vice President’s impeachment trial is ongoing, with the defense panel presenting its witnesses and evidence.

Duterte is accused of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution for allegedly amassing P817 million to P1.5 billion worth of unexplained wealth due to non-declaration of assets and non-divestment in businesses despite a Constitutional ban. —AOL, GMA News
